displayedInputs.question:
Each square in a \(5 \times 5\) grid is either filled or empty, and has up to eight adjacent neighboring squares, where neighboring squares share either a side or a corner. The grid is transformed by the following rules:

• Any filled square with two or three filled neighbors remains filled.

• Any empty square with exactly three filled neighbors becomes a filled square.

• All other squares remain empty or become empty.

A sample transformation is shown in the figure below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Suppose the \(5 \times 5\) grid has a border of empty squares surrounding a \(3 \times 3\) subgrid. How many initial configurations will lead to a transformed grid consisting of a single filled square in the center after a single transformation? (Rotations and reflections of the same configuration are considered different.)

[Figure 2](attached-image-2)

Five rectangles, \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C,\) \(D,\) and \(E,\) are arranged in a square as shown below. These rectangles have dimensions \(1\times6,\) \(2\times4,\) \(5\times6,\) \(2\times7,\) and \(2\times3,\) respectively. (The figure is not drawn to scale.) Which of the five rectangles is the shaded one in the middle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

A rectangle is partitioned into \(5\) regions as shown. Each region is to be painted a solid color - red, orange, yellow, blue, or green - so that regions that touch are painted different colors, and colors can be used more than once. How many different colorings are possible?

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

Suppose that \(13\) cards numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\ldots,\) \(13\) are arranged in a row. The task is to pick them up in numerically increasing order, working repeatedly from left to right. In the example below, cards \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3\) are picked up on the first pass, \(4\) and \(5\) on the second pass, \(6\) on the third pass, \(7,\) \(8,\) \(9,\) \(10\) on the fourth pass, and \(11,\) \(12,\) \(13\) on the fifth pass. For how many of the \(13!\) possible orderings of the cards will the \(13\) cards be picked up in exactly two passes?

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

In rhombus \(ABCD,\) point \(P\) lies on segment \(\overline{AD}\) so that \(\overline{BP} \perp \overline{AD},\) \(AP = 3,\) and \(PD = 2.\) What is the area of \(ABCD?\) (Note: the figure is not drawn to scale.)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

The diagram below shows a rectangle with side lengths \(4\) and \(8\) and a square with side length \(5.\) Three vertices of the square lie on three different sides of the rectangle, as shown. What is the area of the region inside both the square and the rectangle?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

Each square in a \(5 \times 5\) grid is either filled or empty, and has up to eight adjacent neighboring squares, where neighboring squares share either a side or a corner. The grid is transformed by the following rules:

Any filled square with two or three filled neighbors remains filled. Any empty square with exactly three filled neighbors becomes a filled square. All other squares remain empty or become empty.

A sample transformation is shown in the figure below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

Suppose the \(5 \times 5\) grid has a border of empty squares surrounding a \(3 \times 3\) subgrid. How many initial configurations will lead to a transformed grid consisting of a single filled square in the center after a single transformation? (Rotations and reflections of the same configuration are considered different.)

[Figure 2](attached-image-9)

The figure below depicts a regular \(7\)-gon inscribed in a unit circle.

[Figure 1](attached-image-10)

What is the sum of the \(4\)th powers of the lengths of all \(21\) of its edges and diagonals?

mappings.rationale: Treat filled and empty cells as a two-state coloring subject to neighbor-count restrictions, not proper-coloring restrictions. Classify assignments by the initial center state and corner occupancy, checking the required output at all 25 cells and counting orientations separately.
mappings.answerReason: The center condition permits either three initially filled cells or the center plus three others. The four-cell case always produces an unwanted surviving or born cell. With the center initially filled, only its two opposite-corner pairs work. With the center empty, valid triples containing three, two, or one corner number 4, 12, and 4 respectively. Thus the total is 2+4+12+4=22.

mappings.rationale: Add the five rectangular areas to determine the square's side length, then use shared-edge length sums in the pictured arrangement to determine the central rectangle's dimensions.
mappings.answerReason: The total area is 6+8+30+14+6=64, so the square has side 8. The 2×7 rectangle cannot be central. Taking it as the top outer rectangle, its 7-unit boundary side forces the right rectangle to be 1×6. The remaining shared-edge constraints force the left rectangle to be 5×6 and the bottom rectangle to be 3×2. The center is therefore (8-5-1)×(8-2-2)=2×4, rectangle B.

mappings.rationale: Represent touching regions by adjacent vertices. The bottom-middle region touches every other region, while the remaining four regions form a path, allowing a direct multiplication count.
mappings.answerReason: Choose the bottom-middle region's color in 5 ways. After excluding that color, the remaining regions form the path bottom-left, top-left, top-right, bottom-right. Its first region has 4 choices and each subsequent region has 3. The total is 5×4×3³=540.

mappings.rationale: Classify arrangements by the last card k collected on the first pass. Choose the positions occupied by cards 1 through k, with both numerical groups internally increasing, and exclude the arrangement that needs only one pass.
mappings.answerReason: For a fixed first-pass endpoint k, where 1≤k≤12, there are C(13,k) interleavings of the increasing groups 1,...,k and k+1,...,13. Exactly one interleaving is completely increasing and must be excluded. Every valid arrangement has a unique endpoint k, so the count is Σ[C(13,k)-1]=2¹³-2-12=8178.

mappings.rationale: Use equal rhombus sides to identify the hypotenuse of right triangle ABP, find the perpendicular height by the Pythagorean theorem, and calculate base times height.
mappings.answerReason: AD=AP+PD=5, and the rhombus gives AB=5. Since BP is perpendicular to AD, BP=√(5²-3²)=4. Therefore the area is AD×BP=5×4=20.

mappings.rationale: Use the square's perpendicular equal sides and a 3-4-5 right triangle to determine its placement. Similar right triangles determine the horizontal cut, after which the overlap is the square minus its exterior triangular cap.
mappings.answerReason: The square side joining the rectangle's bottom and top rises 4, so its horizontal run is √(25-16)=3. Perpendicular square sides then place the left vertex 3 above the bottom and the exterior vertex 3 above the top. Similarity gives the exterior cap a horizontal base of 4+(3/4)×3=25/4 and height 3. The overlap is 25-(1/2)(25/4)(3)=125/8.

mappings.rationale: Count two-state cell assignments satisfying the simultaneous neighbor-count rules. Separate cases by the initial center state and number of filled corners, enforcing the desired output on the border as well as the central subgrid.
mappings.answerReason: If the center starts filled, the only valid configurations consist of it and one of the two opposite-corner pairs. If the center starts empty, exactly three surrounding cells must be filled; valid triples with three, two, or one corner contribute 4, 12, and 4 configurations. A filled center with three filled neighbors always creates an unwanted output cell. Hence the count is 2+4+12+4=22.

mappings.rationale: Represent the seven unit-circle vertices by seventh roots of unity, so chord lengths become complex moduli. Expand the fourth powers and use cyclic root sums, then remove the double counting of each chord at its two endpoints.
mappings.answerReason: Let ζ=e^(2πi/7). For m=±1,±2, the sum of ζ^(mk) over k=1,...,6 is -1. Since |1-z|⁴=6-4(z+z⁻¹)+z²+z⁻² for |z|=1, the six chords from one vertex contribute 36+8-2=42. Summing over seven vertices counts each chord twice, giving 7×42/2=147.
